Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 15: SECOND MAQABEAN WARRIOR TRIO introduced — three brothers MEBKYUS + MAQABIS + YEHUDA (መብክዩስ፥ መቃቢስ፥ ይሁዳ) given strength by God to save Israel from the Midianite king AKRANDYOS (አክራንድዮስ), who crosses the Jordan with a coalition demanding Israelite tribute (vv. 1-5). The trio is DISTINCT from the five sons of Maqabis in chs 2-4: this is a SEPARATE Maqabean cycle embedded within 1 Mq. **Per Horovitz 1905 p. 195 + scholarly apparatus**: three brothers named **Makabjos, Maqäbjos, and Jehuda** appear at the START OF THE 'SECOND PART' of the FRANKFURT CODEX RÜPPEL II 7 — i.e., what the modern editorial division calls 2 Meqabyan. The phonological closeness to 1 Mq Ch 15 (Mebkyus ≈ Makabjos; Maqabis ≈ Maqäbjos; Yehuda = Jehuda) suggests 1 Mq Ch 15 originated as the OPENING of what is now 2 Mq before the manuscript-tradition's editorial-rearrangement. The verse is a STRUCTURAL-WITNESS to the composite-textual-history of the Meqabyan trilogy.

TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — WRIGHT-VS-FRANKFURT-CODEX TRIPARTITE-VS-BIPARTITE TENSION. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 3(a), Wright's entry X (Orient. 487, item 3) describes the work verbatim as **'The Book of Maccabees ... in three parts'** (Geʽez incipit quoted; cross-referenced to Dillmann *Lex. Aethiop.* Prolegg. p. xi, col. 1 + D'Abbadie *Catalogue Raisonné* no. 55, items 28-30). This is a THIRD INDEPENDENT WITNESS — alongside Dillmann and the EOTC canonical tradition — that the Geʽez Meqabyan was transmitted and understood as a tripartite work. Yet Horovitz 1905 p. 195 reports finding only TWO physically-marked sections in the Frankfurt Codex Rüppel II 7 (the SECOND Maqabean trio Mebkyus + Maqabis + Yehuda introduced at 1 Mq 15:6 per γ.4.8.B entry). This is a GENUINE AND CITABLE SCHOLARLY TENSION rather than a contradiction to be resolved — the British Museum manuscripts evidently presented the work as tripartite; Horovitz's Frankfurt witness did not mark the boundary between the second and third parts. The apparatus's editorial posture ('collection bearing a common title and shared canonical reception ... critical scholarship treats them as compositionally distinct' per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §63) is well-supported by exactly this kind of manuscript-level variation across European-collected Geʽez witnesses.
